Meeting header: 2027-05-04 16:30 PDT | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Helio ML), Jonah Lee (Helio Platform), Sara O'Connor (Helio Product), Raj Patel (Helio Security)

Summary (auto): alignment on which model families to prioritize for the pilot; agreement to run 95th percentile tail tests and to document a hot-swap/emergency pin procedure. Action items captured.

Shared artifacts referenced: Helio pilot benchmarks spreadsheet (link): https://redwood.app/drive/helio/benchmarks-2027-05-03.xlsx; Draft fallback playbook doc: https://redwood.app/docs/helio/fallback-playbook-draft

00:00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick check in, we only have 50 minutes so we'll try to move briskly. Priya, you had a couple updates on new evals?
00:00:12 Priya (Helio): Yeah, thanks. We ran the end-to-end summaries on 10k records, and the latency numbers are.. like, they're okay on the smaller model but quality drops for clinical extraction. we've attached the csv to the sheet. some of the entity spans are missing.
00:00:24 Diego (Redwood SE): Got it. Were those runs using the quantized runtimes or full fp16?
00:00:28 Priya (Helio): Those were fp16 on your hosted API, default settings. We haven't tried your dedicated cluster yet.
00:00:33 Maya (Redwood AE): Right, and that was the thing we wanted to surface — the catalog gap. For Helio's extraction-heavy workload, the mid-sized generative models we tested aren't holding precision. We recommended two paths: (A) move to a higher-quality model variant in the catalog but accept higher token cost and slightly higher latency, or (B) keep the smaller model and add post-processing heuristics.
00:00:52 Sara (Helio Product): From a product POV, our success criteria is 95% extraction F1 on the top-10 entities and P95 latency under 400ms for interactive flows. That's our target.
00:01:05 Jonah (Helio Platform): Just to add, our infra constraint: we need traffic to stay inside our VPC for the private pilot and we require KMS-backed key management. So any plan that implies sending raw PII out of VPC is non-starter.
00:01:18 Raj (Helio Security): And we will need SOC2 attestation plus audit logs for model prompts and inference traces. We also prefer RBAC keys over generic tokens.
00:01:27 Maya (Redwood AE): Understood, we'll surface our Private deployment options. The Redwood Private control plane supports customer-managed VPC peering and KMS integration — we'll include the SOC2 artifacts.
00:01:36 Diego (Redwood SE): On the model side, a few notes: the catalog has a slightly larger model family that preserves entity spans better — but it's heavier. We can run it in a dedicated pool with autoscaling to keep P95 steady. Also, the runtime supports prefix K V caching for repeated prompts which could drop cost and latency for many of your repeated templates.
00:01:54 Priya (Helio): Wait — kv cache spelling — is that K V cache? we saw mention of K V cash in the doc earlier.
00:02:00 Diego (Redwood SE): Yeah, KV cache, sorry — sometimes the transcription says K V cash. It's a key-value cache for prefix keys that dramatically cuts token work for repeated user templates.
00:02:07 Maya (Redwood AE): The next bit we need to decide is pin policy. If we pin to the larger model to hit F1 we pay more and lose some headroom; if we pin to the smaller model we need fallback tooling and post-processing. We recommend a soft-pin: live canary on 5% traffic to the larger model, 95% on smaller with rerank for extraction.
00:02:26 Priya (Helio): Can you define "soft-pin" again?
00:02:29 Diego (Redwood SE): Soft-pin is where you pin a variant in the catalog as preferred, but the routing rules allow automated fallback to a compatible variant if capacity or latency thresholds are breached. Think of it as preferred->failover.
00:02:41 Speaker 1: there was also the idea of shadow testing the larger model for 24h to measure regressions without impacting traffic.
00:02:50 Sara (Helio Product): Shadow testing sounds good. But our timeline — we need a pilot decision by end of next week to align with the mobile release. So we can't stretch too long.
00:03:02 Maya (Redwood AE): Okay timer-wise that gives us about 7 days. Practical plan: run shadow and a single canary, do 24h bulk evals with your sample traffic, then tabletop a hot-swap.
00:03:13 Jonah (Helio Platform): On canary routing — what are the escape hatches? If the larger model spikes latency we need to swap back quickly. How long to fail-over?
00:03:21 Diego (Redwood SE): With the right routing policy and health checks, you can cut traffic to the variant within seconds. But there are warmup costs for KV cache and initial cold-starts. To be safe we recommend a deadman's switch: an automated rule that flips traffic to a known-good fallback if the P95 exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive minutes.
00:03:38 Priya (Helio): Is that configurable per-route? We have different SLOs for interactive vs batch.
00:03:42 Diego (Redwood SE): Yep, per-route policies, per-model thresholds. You can also set different cache warming delays and prefer a gradual ramp-down.
00:03:50 Raj (Helio Security): From security — any logs we keep for auditing, are they redactable? We cannot store raw PHI.
00:03:55 Maya (Redwood AE): Good point. We have redaction hooks and token filtering; we can also route only extracted metadata to logs. We'll send the SOC2/PII redaction playbook.
00:04:05 Sara (Helio Product): Back to model selection — Diego, you suggested trying quantization? Would that help keep the bigger model under our latency SLO?
00:04:12 Diego (Redwood SE): Possibly. Quantization can reduce memory and improve throughput but it sometimes impacts extraction fidelity. We should run A/B on quantized vs fp16 for your extraction eval set. That's one of the tests Diego will run.
00:04:25 Maya (Redwood AE): Ok so concrete experiments this week: (1) tail-latency runs for 95th pct using 512 context window on both small and large variants with quantized and fp16; (2) 24h shadow run of large variant against production-like sample; (3) tabletop hot-swap drill next Tues 11 May.
00:04:42 Priya (Helio): We'll upload a 24h anonymized sample by Wednesday EOD.
00:04:46 Jonah (Helio Platform): We'll also export our SLO doc and the traffic mix.
00:04:50 Maya (Redwood AE): Great. On the fallback playbook — the doc linked has a recommended sequence: canary -> monitor 1h -> if P95>threshold initiate deadman's switch -> rollback and warm fallback. We'll add a step for cache-warm prepopulation to reduce cold-start pain.
00:05:05 Speaker 2: (murmur) sounds good.
00:05:10 Diego (Redwood SE): Small caveat: some of the smaller models in the catalog don't have architectures compatible with the larger family for a true binary fallback; in those cases we need a rewriter layer or a shim to translate format differences. That's a catalog gap we flagged.
00:05:25 Priya (Helio): So you're saying we might not have a drop-in fallback and would need to post-process?
00:05:29 Diego (Redwood SE): Exactly. We'll map compatibility matrix and flag where we need transform logic.
00:05:34 Maya (Redwood AE): We'll include that compatibility matrix in the deck. Action: Diego to produce catalog compatibility map for Helio's top 3 flows.
00:05:42 Diego (Redwood SE): Noted.
00:05:45 Sara (Helio Product): One other ask — can we get token-level cost and approximate per-endpoint spend so we can model pricing for our finance team?
00:05:53 Maya (Redwood AE): Yes, we'll provide an estimated cost model — token-level breakdown, expected dedicated pool baseline, and a delta for adding the larger model on canary. I'll send a spreadsheet with scenarios.
00:06:02 Priya (Helio): Also curious about benchmarking against Anthropic / OpenAI. Are those in scope?
00:06:08 Maya (Redwood AE): We can include them for reference. We won't run them inside your VPC, but we can show public benchmarks. Keep in mind differences in privacy and E2E control.
00:06:18 Raj (Helio Security): make sure you list where data leaves our control. we need that spelled out for sign off.
00:06:23 Maya (Redwood AE): Absolutely. We'll list flow diagrams and boundary conditions.
00:06:28 Speaker 3: brief pause
00:06:40 Maya (Redwood AE): Any blockers we haven't discussed?
00:06:44 Priya (Helio): Speed of decision — we need final pilot configuration by next Friday or we miss the mobile push.
00:06:49 Maya (Redwood AE): Understood. We'll prioritize the latency spreadsheet and the compatibility map.
00:06:55 Diego (Redwood SE): I'll run the tail tests tonight and upload results by 5/7. Note: the 95th pct run may show higher variance immediately after swaps due to cold KV cache. I'll include both cold and warmed runs.
00:07:08 Jonah (Helio Platform): For the hot-swap drill, can Redwood lead the runbook and we observe?
00:07:13 Maya (Redwood AE): Yes we'll lead and we'll provide the runbook beforehand. We'll simulate canary fail and measure time to restore.
00:07:19 Priya (Helio): Good. Anything else?
00:07:23 Maya (Redwood AE): Quick recap of owners and dates — Maya: cost spreadsheet (5/6); Diego: tail runs + compatibility map (5/7); Helio: traffic sample + SLO doc (5/5); Raj: security confirmation (5/10); schedule hot-swap tabletop 5/11.
00:07:41 Sara (Helio Product): That works. Also please add notes on redaction — we must not store raw PHI in logs.
00:07:48 Maya (Redwood AE): We'll include PII redaction and audit log options.
00:07:52 Speaker 1: okay thanks all
00:07:55 Maya (Redwood AE): We'll follow up with an email with links to the artifacts and next steps. Thanks everyone.
